questions.source_title: Outokumpu: What makes stainless steel corrosion resistant?
questions.use: Original factual synopsis for local reference; no full article or training import.
questions: Why does chromium improve corrosion resistance in steel?
Why does chromium improve corrosion resistance?
Why is stainless steel corrosion resistant?
How does chromium protect stainless steel?
questions.answer: Chromium enables stainless steel to form a thin passive surface film in oxidizing environments. That film limits corrosion reactions at the underlying metal. Protection depends on the alloy and exposure: aggressive conditions can break down the film and cause localized or uniform corrosion. Chromium therefore does not make every steel immune to corrosion, and this mechanism alone does not establish a corrosion rate or service life.
